sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Breda is using price to pull visitors into its garages and is widening paid parking outward. The council's 2026 parking-tax ordinance, in force from 19 December 2025 with the levy applying from 1 January 2026, sets on-street parking at 2.70 euros an hour in the Centrumzone and 1.80 euros in the Singelzone [2]. Since 1 January 2025 paid parking has been simplified into two zones, inside and outside the singels, with paid parking reported to be extended to more neighbourhoods [3]. Paid hours in the central areas run Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 01:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 01:00, and in the outer neighbourhoods to 22:00 [4]. In February 2023 the city cut garage tariffs by 12 to 14 cents an hour and said it wants visitors in garages rather than on streets [5].

The 2026 tariffs make the first resident permit free and the second 8 euros a month; the city's permit page says that from 1 January 2027 the second permit becomes free across Breda [11]. Paid parking in the Tuinzigt-Slingerweg neighbourhood is postponed to 1 March 2027, after the 1 January 2027 policy change, because the city's counts showed spaces almost fully occupied at many times [14]. The 2026-2030 coalition agreement, after the council decision of 2 July 2026, plans the free second permit and a 30 km/h limit inside the singels [12]. The pedestrian area is open to traffic only at set times, enforced by cameras [16], and inside the singels a low-emission zone bars trucks of emission class 0 to 5, with a zero-emission zone for vans and trucks scheduled from 1 January 2029 [17].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The coalition agreement is a plan, not yet built: it earmarks 2 million euros plus 0.5 million per year for a mobility hub on the edge of the centre, 5.5 million euros to refurbish garage Oranje Zuid and 4 million euros for a better parking route information system, and says a garage is to be built at Gasthuisvelden [13]. In the car-light Havenkwartier the city plans a parking hub at Steenen Hoofd, with only 29 permits for the first building until then [15]. The five municipal garages list 40 charging points, operated by 50five and usable only with a charging pass [10]. Chasséveld, Beyerd-Vlaszak and Gasthuisvelden are open-air car parks near the centre with 653, 365 and 335 spaces, and Chasséveld is closed for events about ten weeks a year [8].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The city's five municipal garages, Barones, Chassé Parking, Oranje Zuid, Het Turfschip and De Prins, all list the same tariff of 2.36 euros an hour, 14 euros per 24 hours and an evening maximum of 5.50 euros, and have 2,638 spaces in total on the city's pages [0][1]. Interparking announced on 14 April 2026 that from 1 July 2026 it will manage the five garages, which it puts at 2,655 spaces; we have only the announcement [6]. The garages use number plate recognition, with office, night and resident subscriptions [7]. Q-Park runs three sites: Centrum (360 spaces) and the station-side P+R Station (720) and P+R Stationsweg (89), with no standard tariffs online [9].

Our data cover only the two Q-Park park-and-rides, 822 spaces, measured for about 8 weeks since 22 August 2026; none of the municipal garages is in our feed. Occupancy averaged about 30% on weekdays and 27% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The small Stationsweg site (94 spaces in the feed) is much fuller than P+R Station (728): 62% on weekdays against 26%, and it reached full in a single Tuesday-morning reading. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
